title_en: The disputants who came to Dawud
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The ayah asks whether the news of the disputants has reached the hearer, when they climbed into the mihrab.

They entered upon Dawud and he was alarmed at them; they said: do not fear, we are a pair of disputants, one of us has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth, do not be unjust, and guide us to the right path.
One of them said: this is my brother, he has ninety-nine ewes and I have one ewe; he said to entrust it to him, and he overcame me in speech.
Dawud said: he has wronged you by asking for your ewe to add to his ewes; many partners wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they.
Dawud thought that We had tested him; he asked forgiveness of his Lord, fell down bowing, and turned to God.
God forgave him that, and said that he has nearness to Us and a good place of return.

chapters.summary_md: A pair of disputants came to Dawud with a case about one ewe and ninety-nine ewes, and Dawud gave judgement [c2][c3][c4]. Dawud thought that he had been tested, asked forgiveness, fell down bowing and turned to God, and God forgave him [c5][c6].
chapters.body_md:
The ayah asks whether the news of the disputants has reached the hearer, when they climbed into the mihrab [c1]. They entered upon Dawud and he was alarmed at them [c2]. They said: do not fear, we are a pair of disputants, one of us has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth, do not be unjust, and guide us to the right path [c2].

One of them said: this is my brother, he has ninety-nine ewes and I have one ewe; he said to entrust it to him, and he overcame me in speech [c3]. Dawud said: he has wronged you by asking for your ewe to add to his ewes; many partners wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they [c4].

Dawud thought that We had tested him; he asked forgiveness of his Lord, fell down bowing, and turned to God [c5]. God forgave him that, and said that he has nearness to Us and a good place of return [c6].
chapters.deep_md: Dawud's answer speaks of partners in general and then names the exceptions, those who believe and do righteous deeds [c4]. The ayah does not say what Dawud was forgiven; it says only that God forgave him that [c5][c6]. The same ayah that gives his judgement gives his turning to God, so the case and the test are told together [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: A pair of people came to Dawud with an argument about sheep: one had ninety-nine and the other had one [c2][c3]. Dawud gave his answer, then asked God to forgive him and bowed down, and God forgave him [c4][c5][c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the case teaches that many who share a thing wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds [c4]. Another is that the passage ends with turning to God and with forgiveness [c5][c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the disputants were, whether they were people or something else, or how they entered; the ayah says only that they climbed into the mihrab.
- Not established: what Dawud thought was the test, or what he was forgiven; the ayah says that without naming it.
- Not established: whether the case is a real dispute or a parable; the ayah does not say.
- Not established: where or when this was, or what Dawud did after the judgement.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on this case and on the meaning of the test. None is used in this draft.

Later commentators gave many accounts of what the test was; none is in the ayat and none is used here. A scholar should decide how the page should word the phrase that Dawud thought We had tested him (zanna anna-ma fatannahu).
On etiquette, this draft gives no verdict on Dawud; it states what the ayat state, that he asked forgiveness and was forgiven.
